title: Navigation bar active-state variant matrix (12 variants)

color.method: Pixel sampling via median-cut quantization of the supplied JPEG/GIF (compressed images, so values are approximate within a few units). Entries marked 'approx' were judged by eye, not sampled.
color.roles: Achromatic; one near-black fill marks active.

observed.layout: Two columns by six rows of identical 4-item bars (home, filter, profile, settings) in rounded rectangles. Each variant is labeled in tiny text: simple, icon simple, icon circle, icon rectangle, icon underline, text simple, text circle, text rectangle, text underline, expandable, elevated rectangle, elevated circle.
observed.hierarchy: Reads as a specimen sheet: label above each variant, same bar repeated.
observed.iconography: Monoline outline icons; the active icon becomes filled.
observed.materials: Flat grey capsules; 'elevated' variants lift the active circle/rectangle above the bar edge.

implementation_notes: Taxonomy of indicator shapes: none, circle, rounded rectangle, underline, expand (icon+label), elevated.
Dimensions combine two axes: content (icon / text / both) and indicator (none / circle / rect / underline / elevated).
Elevated variants need the bar to allow overflow above its top edge.
interpretation.caveat: Taxonomy as a lens is Claude's synthesis.

concept_work.essence: A systematic exploration of how one nav component can signal active state, holding everything else constant.
what_makes_it_work: Controlled comparison: only one variable changes per row, which makes trade-offs visible.
gaps_to_make_it_work: No guidance on when to choose which variant.
Text-only variants lose icon recognition; underline-only is subtle.
No states beyond active (pressed, disabled, badge).

lessons: Explore a component along orthogonal axes (content type x indicator shape) instead of making random variations.
A specimen sheet is itself a valuable dataset format.
confidence: high for structure, low for exact colors
